COMS W4130.title: Principles and Practice of Parallel Programming
COMS W4130.description: Studies parallel programming techniques, performance analysis and implementation of concurrent algorithms.
COMS W4130.note: The archive calls for data structures and basic algorithm analysis. Java experience is also needed with W3136. The current Statistics Bulletin still lists W4130 as a Data Science elective. Consult the department for availability.

COMS W4180.title: Network Security
COMS W4180.description: An introduction to security principles for networks, including authentication, cryptography and defensive protocols.
COMS W4180.note: Archived sections expect networking and sockets programming. One archived section also names older data structures course W3139. Check the department for current equivalents.

COMS W4160.pre: COMS W3134/COMS W3136/COMS W3137;COMS W3251/MATH UN2010/MATH UN2015
COMS W4160.note: The Bulletin requires a strong programming background and familiarity with linear algebra. The graph shows example linear algebra courses.

COMS W4121.note: The probability or algorithms course may be taken concurrently or satisfied with equivalent preparation. The listing also expects computer organization and working C or C++ knowledge.

CSEE W4121.note: The graph shows representative computer organization preparation. The listing also expects working C or C++ knowledge and accepts equivalent probability preparation.

BMCS E4575.note: The listing calls for machine learning, multivariable calculus and linear algebra alongside strong Python or R skills.

EECS E6791.note: The current designators for the named courses are ECBM E4040 and ELEN E4620. The listing accepts comparable courses and also expects machine learning, linear algebra, probability and statistics background.

EECS E6792.note: The listed prerequisites can be met through comparable courses. Machine learning, linear algebra, probability, statistics and working Python knowledge are also expected.

ELEN E4620.title: Numerical Methods for Data Analysis
ELEN E4620.description: Introduces numerical linear algebra and applications to data fitting, clustering and dimensionality reduction.
ELEN E4620.note: The instructor expects the ability to write short scripts in Python, Julia, MATLAB or a similar language.

MECS E4603.title: Applied Robotics: Algorithms and Software
MECS E4603.description: Applies software and algorithms to robot motion, manipulation, spatial reasoning and control.

MECS E6616.note: The prose lists the three robotics courses as alternatives. The structured Bulletin text is inconsistent. Confirm equivalent preparation for the section.

POLS GU4730.note: The department accepts equivalent calculus preparation. Instructor permission is required.

MATH GR5010.note: The listing includes legacy designators and accepts equivalents for preparation in multivariable calculus, differential equations and probability.

PHIL GU4337.title: Early Twentieth Century Philosophy
PHIL GU4337.description: Studies key work in early twentieth-century philosophy. The fall 2025 section focused on Frank Ramsey.
PHIL GU4337.note: The department lists this seminar for advanced undergraduates and graduate students.

PHIL GU4424.title: Modal Logic
PHIL GU4424.description: Studies formal systems for reasoning about necessity and possibility.
PHIL GU4424.note: Barnard’s archived joint catalogue asks for a term of formal logic. Columbia’s current course card gives no preparation details. Verify the section’s rule.

PHIL UN3611.description: Discussion section for PHIL UN3601 when required by the offering.
